automotive.title: EV Range Prediction

energy.title: Industrial Waste-Heat Recovery
energy.preview: Steel mills, cement plants and other energy-intensive industries release large amounts of thermal energy through furnaces, kilns, …
energy.desc: Steel mills, cement plants and other energy-intensive industries release large amounts of thermal energy through furnaces, kilns, exhaust gases, clinker cooling and hot surfaces. Much of this heat is discharged even though it originated from valuable fuel or electricity.
techScope: Recover waste heat and convert it into electricity, process heat, cooling or stored thermal energy.
Do so economically.
Avoid negatively affecting the primary industrial process.
deliverables: Concept design for a heat-recovery system.
Estimated recoverable energy and economics.
Analysis of impact on the primary process.

energy.title: Industrial Loads as Renewable-Energy Storage
energy.preview: Surplus renewable electricity does not always need to be stored in batteries.
energy.desc: Surplus renewable electricity does not always need to be stored in batteries. Some industrial processes, including thermal processes, cold storage, compressors and batch operations, have electricity demand that may be shifted in time without proportionally reducing production.
techScope: Identify which industrial processes can act as flexible demand.
Quantify how much consumption can shift toward high renewable generation.
Ensure production and product quality are not affected.
deliverables: Ranked list of flexible industrial processes.
Estimate of shiftable load.
Scheduling approach that protects production and quality.

energy.title: Long-Duration Renewable-Energy Storage Beyond Conventional Batteries
energy.preview: As renewable penetration increases, electricity may need to be stored for days or longer.
energy.desc: As renewable penetration increases, electricity may need to be stored for days or longer. Simply adding more lithium-ion batteries increases cost, material requirements, thermal-management needs and system complexity.
techScope: Explore alternative or hybrid storage approaches for storage over days or longer.
Evaluate efficiency, safety, lifetime and environmental performance.
Assess economics.
deliverables: Comparison of candidate long-duration storage options.
Recommended approach with efficiency and cost estimates.
Safety, lifetime and environmental assessment.

energy.title: Hydropower Turbine Erosion from Sediment
energy.preview: Rivers carry suspended sand, silt and other abrasive particles.
energy.desc: Rivers carry suspended sand, silt and other abrasive particles. When sediment passes through hydropower turbines at high velocity, it erodes blades and runner surfaces, reducing efficiency and increasing maintenance and replacement.
techScope: Protect turbines in sediment-heavy rivers from progressive erosion.
Maintain high energy-conversion efficiency.
Avoid frequent replacement or major alteration of river flow.
deliverables: Erosion-mitigation concept (design, coating or operation).
Analysis or test of erosion resistance.
Assessment of efficiency and maintenance impact.

energy.title: Renewable Energy During Cyclones — Shut Down or Survive?
energy.preview: Solar farms, wind turbines and electrical infrastructure can experience extreme wind, flooding, debris impact and rapid environmen…
energy.desc: Solar farms, wind turbines and electrical infrastructure can experience extreme wind, flooding, debris impact and rapid environmental change during cyclones. Designing every component only for the maximum possible load substantially increases installation cost.
techScope: Predict approaching extreme weather.
Dynamically change operating or physical configuration to reduce damage.
Reduce reliance on stronger and more expensive structures.
deliverables: Concept or prototype for weather-triggered protective response.
Comparison of damage or cost versus fixed strong design.
Decision logic for shutdown versus survival configuration.

energy.title: Can Solar and Wind Share the Same Grid Connection?
energy.preview: Solar peaks during the day while wind may occur at different times, so transmission connections and substations remain underutilis…
energy.desc: Solar peaks during the day while wind may occur at different times, so transmission connections and substations remain underutilised for significant portions of the day.
techScope: Share transmission capacity, substations and power-conversion infrastructure between solar and wind.
Increase utilisation of existing grid connections.
Avoid congestion, instability and power-quality problems.
deliverables: Model of combined solar-wind generation on one connection.
Utilisation improvement estimate.
Analysis of congestion and power-quality risks.

energy.title: Renewable-Energy Cybersecurity
energy.preview: Modern renewable plants depend on sensors, digital controllers, remote monitoring, communication networks and software-based energ…
energy.desc: Modern renewable plants depend on sensors, digital controllers, remote monitoring, communication networks and software-based energy-management systems. A cyberattack or corrupted sensor signal could cause incorrect control decisions in a grid-connected system.
techScope: Detect malicious or abnormal control commands and corrupted sensor data.
Continue operating safely when communication or monitoring is compromised.
Keep cost and computational complexity low.
deliverables: Detection method with test results on injected attacks and corrupted data.
Safe-operation fallback strategy.
Cost and complexity assessment. ---

designtextiles.title: PFAS-Free Oil-Repellent Finish for the Apparel Industry
designtextiles.preview: Oil and stain-repellent finishes on workwear, aprons and outdoor apparel have relied on PFAS "forever chemicals", which are being …
designtextiles.desc: Oil and stain-repellent finishes on workwear, aprons and outdoor apparel have relied on PFAS "forever chemicals", which are being phased out globally due to bioaccumulation and health risks. Most affordable alternatives repel water well but perform poorly against oil, which has much lower surface tension. Can a fluorine-free finish reach oil-repellency close enough to PFAS to be commercially viable for apparel?
techScope: Trial 2–3 fluorine-free chemistries (silicone-based, wax-dispersion, bio-based plant-wax or stearic-acid derivative) on standard woven cotton or cotton-poly fabric, applied by pad-dry-cure.
Test oil repellency (AATCC 118 style 1–8 rating), water contact angle, wash durability at 0/5/10/20 washes, and hand-feel or stiffness.
Benchmark against an untreated control and, if accessible, a PFAS-treated reference.
deliverables: Comparison table: finish type × oil-repellency rating × wash durability × cost per metre × hand-feel score.
Recommendation on which fluorine-free option comes closest to PFAS performance for apparel.
Note on the biggest remaining performance gap, usually wash durability.

designtextiles.title: Alternative for Metal Safety-Pin Hangtags That Put Holes in Garments
designtextiles.preview: Retail tags are almost universally attached with metal safety pins or plastic barbs that pierce fabric.
designtextiles.desc: Retail tags are almost universally attached with metal safety pins or plastic barbs that pierce fabric. On delicate fabrics such as silk, fine cotton, knitwear and premium handloom, this leaves permanent pinholes or snag marks. Can a non-piercing method hold a tag securely through in-store handling while leaving zero permanent mark?
techScope: Design and test 2–3 non-piercing mechanisms: elastic loop-and-slot tag, micro-clip with softened jaws, and removable low-tack adhesive-tab tag.
Test pull force to failure, reattachment count (10–20 cycles), handling simulation (folding, hanging, trying on), fabric damage under magnification, and cost per tag.
Benchmark against a standard safety-pin tag.
deliverables: Comparison table: attachment method × pull force × reattachment durability × visible fabric damage × cost per unit.
Recommendation on the best "same security, zero damage" method.
Guidance on which fabric types (delicate versus sturdy) each option suits.

designtextiles.title: Alternative Mosquito-Repellent Treatment for Sleeping Bags and Camping Textiles
designtextiles.preview: Permethrin is the industry-standard insect-repellent treatment for camping textiles but is toxic to aquatic life and cats, persist…
designtextiles.desc: Permethrin is the industry-standard insect-repellent treatment for camping textiles but is toxic to aquatic life and cats, persistent in the environment, and leaves residue on skin-contact fabric. Natural repellents such as citronella, neem and eucalyptus oils lose effectiveness within hours on fabric. Can a plant-based repellent be bound to fabric with enough durability and slow release for a multi-night trip?
techScope: Test 2–3 delivery methods on sleeping-bag-liner fabric: microencapsulated essential-oil finish, neem-oil pad-dry-cure finish, and a replaceable herb sachet in the lining.
Measure repellency (landing-rate field bioassay or lab partnership) at 0, 8 and 24 hours and after washing, plus scent tolerability and wash durability at 0/5/10 washes.
Add a literature-based environmental comparison against Permethrin; benchmark against untreated and, if accessible, permethrin-treated fabric.
deliverables: Comparison table: treatment × repellency duration × landing-rate reduction × wash durability × scent rating × environmental impact.
Conclusion on which method gets closest to Permethrin's effectiveness window.
Honest note on the remaining durability gap.

designtextiles.title: Distinguishing Genuine Handloom from Machine-Made Imitations and Making Weaver Stories Visible
designtextiles.preview: Genuine handloom is hard for customers to tell apart from machine-made imitations, and weavers' stories rarely reach the buyer.
designtextiles.desc: Genuine handloom is hard for customers to tell apart from machine-made imitations, and weavers' stories rarely reach the buyer. Can a low-cost, weaver-friendly system verify authenticity and show the weaver's story at the point of purchase without expensive technology or literacy barriers?
techScope: Authenticity: a tamper-evident physical marker (unique thread pattern, QR label or hologram-plus-QR) linked to a database record of weaver, loom, date and product; customer scans the QR to verify.
Story layer: the same scan shows a weaver profile (name, region, experience, photo, note on the piece), with a simple intake method such as phone or voice-note collection for low-literacy weavers.
Test tag-forgery resistance, scan reliability across phones and lighting, weaver onboarding usability, customer willingness to pay, and cost per unit.
deliverables: Working prototype: physical tag or QR sample plus a web page showing verification status and weaver story.
Forgery-resistance test result.
Customer willingness-to-pay survey comparing tagged versus untagged items.

designtextiles.title: Campus-Waste-to-Composite: Turning Campus Leaf Litter and Plastic Waste into Usable Panels
designtextiles.preview: The campus continuously generates dry leaf litter (swept and often burned or dumped) and plastic waste, with no on-campus value-recovery pathway.
designtextiles.desc: The campus continuously generates dry leaf litter (swept and often burned or dumped) and plastic waste, with no on-campus value-recovery pathway. Shredded leaf fibre with shredded plastic as the binding matrix could form a usable composite. Can such a panel reach useful strength for a low-load campus application using zero external raw material?
techScope: Prepare leaf fibre and single-type shredded plastic (LDPE or PET); heat-press composites at varied leaf-to-plastic ratios (e.g. 20/80, 40/60, 60/40).
Test flexural or impact strength against a plastic-only panel, water absorption and swelling, and 2–3 weeks of outdoor UV exposure.
Account for waste volume consumed and possible campus applications (signage boards, garden edging or pavers, planters, common-room accent panels).
deliverables: Working composite panel or tile prototype made entirely from campus-collected waste.
Strength and water-resistance comparison table across fibre ratios.
Waste-diversion estimate (kg of waste per panel and share of monthly waste offset).

designtextiles.title: AI-Powered Business Assistant for Fashion MSMEs (Trend Forecasting + Dynamic Pricing + More)
designtextiles.preview: Small fashion MSMEs cannot afford the trend-forecasting, dynamic-pricing and customer-analytics tools used by large brands, althou…
designtextiles.desc: Small fashion MSMEs cannot afford the trend-forecasting, dynamic-pricing and customer-analytics tools used by large brands, although the underlying signals are free or near-free. The gap is that nobody has bundled these into one affordable assistant. Can a lightweight modular assistant give MSMEs insight on what to make, what to charge and how to sell, using free data and simple explainable models?
techScope: Module 1, trend engine: hashtag frequency, Google Trends and public bestseller lists, with a pretrained vision model extracting colour and garment category; rising/falling dashboard with lead-time metric.

Module 2, pricing assistant: rule-based scoring from competitor price, trend direction and stock level, giving a suggested price range. Module 3, sentiment and return-reason analyzer: buckets feedback into fit, fabric feel, colour mismatch, delivery delay and praise. Module 4 (optional): production-planning bridge to fabric quantity.
Validate with backtests for trend and pricing, agreement percentage for sentiment, and a usability test with a real MSME owner.
deliverables: Working dashboard combining at least 2 of the 3 core modules.
Separately reported backtested accuracy for each module.
Written case study using any brand data as real-world validation.

designtextiles.title: Fragrance-Blended Reflective Coat for Sanitary Workers
designtextiles.preview: Sanitation workers face low visibility near traffic during early-morning and night shifts, and constant exposure to malodour that …
designtextiles.desc: Sanitation workers face low visibility near traffic during early-morning and night shifts, and constant exposure to malodour that affects wellbeing and public perception of the job. Reflective vests and odour treatments exist separately but not combined. Can a reflective safety coat carry a long-lasting, wash-durable fragrance or odour-neutralising treatment without either function compromising the other?
techScope: Reflective part: standard retroreflective tape on hi-vis fabric at chest, back and arms.
Odour part: microencapsulated fragrance finish, or an odour-neutralising finish (activated charcoal or zinc-ricinoleate type), ideally a neutralising base layer plus a light fragrance top-note.
Test reflectivity retention, odour neutralisation against a real malodour source, fragrance longevity at 0/8 hours and post-wash, reflective-tape wash durability at 10–15 washes, and wearer comfort.
deliverables: Working coat or vest prototype with both functions integrated.
Reflectivity-retention comparison, treated versus untreated.
Odour-neutralisation rating across time (0 hr / 8 hr / post-wash) and wearer-acceptance survey result.

designtextiles.title: Anti-Static + Flame-Resistant Coverall for Fuel Station and LPG Workers
designtextiles.preview: Fuel-station and LPG workers face fire risk from static discharge near fuel vapour, yet most wear polyester-blend uniforms that bu…
designtextiles.desc: Fuel-station and LPG workers face fire risk from static discharge near fuel vapour, yet most wear polyester-blend uniforms that build static and can melt onto skin. Industrial anti-static and flame-resistant coveralls exist but are expensive imports. Can a locally producible coverall reach static-dissipation and flame-resistance performance close to commercial standards at a fraction of the cost?
techScope: Anti-static: continuous grid of conductive thread (stainless-steel or metal-coated) every 2–3 cm in cotton or cotton-poly fabric.
Flame resistance: non-halogenated phosphorus/nitrogen FR finish by pad-dry-cure at 2–3 concentrations, balancing protection with fabric stiffness.
Test static-charge decay, vertical flame test (char length, afterflame), performance after 0/5/10 washes, wearer comfort, and cost versus imported coveralls.
deliverables: Coverall or fabric-panel prototype with both treatments integrated.
Static-decay and flame-test result tables, treated versus untreated, across wash cycles.
Cost comparison against commercial alternatives.

designtextiles.title: Natural-Fibre-Reinforced Composite Blade for Small Wind Turbines
designtextiles.preview: Even micro wind-turbine blades are usually glass or carbon-fibre composite, which are expensive and non-biodegradable.
designtextiles.desc: Even micro wind-turbine blades are usually glass or carbon-fibre composite, which are expensive and non-biodegradable. Natural fibres such as jute, coir, sisal and banana are cheap and locally abundant in India but rarely tested for blades, where stiffness-to-weight and fatigue matter most. Can a natural-fibre composite blade be a viable low-cost alternative for low-load micro-turbines?
techScope: Hand-layup jute fabric with resin (epoxy, or bio-resin if accessible) in a mould for a 30–60 cm blade, with an identical glass-fibre control.
Test tip deflection, weight, RPM versus wind speed on an identical hub, fatigue by repeated flexing, and moisture absorption.
Document moisture-resistance limits and a mitigation such as a protective coating.
deliverables: Working jute-composite blade prototype and glass-fibre control.
Stiffness, weight and RPM-versus-wind-speed comparison.
Documented moisture-resistance limitations with a suggested mitigation.

designtextiles.title: Thermoreversible Adhesive Seams for Easier Garment Disassembly and Recycling
designtextiles.preview: Stitched seams make garments hard to disassemble for recycling.
designtextiles.desc: Stitched seams make garments hard to disassemble for recycling. A heat-activated adhesive seam that holds through normal wear and washing but releases cleanly at a higher controlled temperature could enable recycling. Can an off-the-shelf heat-activated adhesive prove this at prototype scale?
techScope: Use commercially available hot-melt film or webbing (fusible bonding web type) or low-melt hot-glue to bond two fabric panels with a household iron or heat press.

Test bond strength versus a stitched seam, wash durability over 5–10 washes, controlled release at a higher temperature with residue scoring, recovered-fabric quality, and the temperature margin between wash/iron and release.
deliverables: Bonded (not stitched) fabric-panel prototype.
Bond-strength comparison against stitched seams and a wash-durability result.
Controlled-release demonstration showing clean separation at a defined higher temperature.

designtextiles.title: Phase-Change-Material (PCM) Thermoregulating Fabric
designtextiles.preview: Textile finishes containing microencapsulated phase-change materials can absorb and release heat to buffer wearer temperature.
designtextiles.desc: Textile finishes containing microencapsulated phase-change materials can absorb and release heat to buffer wearer temperature. This is referenced elsewhere in the Textile set and is drafted here as a placeholder pending confirmation with the circle.
techScope: Apply microencapsulated PCM to fabric by pad-dry-cure.
Test thermal buffering, wash durability and hand-feel against untreated fabric.
deliverables: Treated-fabric prototype.
Thermal-performance and wash-durability comparison.
Cost and applicability note.
